message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how you can create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that is equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (if it were available) and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
Because Google Cloud does not currently offer the RTX A6000 as a GPU type, the example uses the closest supported GPU – **NVIDIA Tesla A100** – but the same pattern applies to any GPU that Google Cloud supports.

---

## 1.  Prerequisites

| Item | How to set it up |
|------|------------------|
| **Google Cloud Project** | Create a project in the Cloud Console or use an existing one. |
| **Billing enabled** | Make sure billing is attached to the project. |
| **API enabled** | Enable the *Compute Engine API* (`https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1`) in the Cloud Console. |
| **Service account** | Create a service account with the `roles/compute.admin` role (or a custom role that includes `compute.instances.create`). Download its JSON key. |
| **gcloud SDK** | Install the Cloud SDK (`curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash`) and run `gcloud init`. |

---

## 2.  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣ Authenticate with your service account
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=/path/to/key.json

# 2️⃣ Set the project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
gcloud config set project $PROJECT_ID
gcloud config set compute/zone $ZONE

# 3️⃣ Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \        # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \       # Official Ubuntu image project
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \                # Size of the boot disk
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \               # SSD persistent disk
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \   # GPU type & count
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \          # Keep the instance running during maintenance
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \ # Optional: custom startup script
  --tags=http-server,https-server \        # Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

> **Note**  
> Replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with the actual GPU type you want if it becomes available.  
> The `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` line is optional; it lets you run custom commands after the instance boots.

---

## 3.  Using the REST API (HTTP)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), you can do so with a simple `POST` request. Below is a **JSON payload** that you would send to the endpoint:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-4"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Making the HTTP request

```bash
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# 1️⃣ Get an OAuth 2.0 access token
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣ POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance-config.json
```

> **Tip**  
> Save the JSON payload above to a file called `instance-config.json` and reference it with `-d @instance-config.json`.

---

## 4.  Verifying the Instance

After the instance is created, you can verify its status:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-demo
```

Look for the `status` field (`PROVISIONING`, `RUNNING`, etc.) and the `accelerators` section to confirm the GPU has been attached.

---

## 5.  Cleaning Up

To avoid incurring charges, delete the instance when you’re done:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-demo --quiet
```

---

## 6.  Quick Reference (Table)

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `name` | `rtx-a6000-demo` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | `n1-standard-8` | 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM |
| `bootDiskSizeGb` | `200` | Size of the boot disk |
| `bootDiskType` | `pd-ssd` | SSD persistent disk |
| `imageFamily` | `ubuntu-2004-lts` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| `imageProject` | `ubuntu-os-cloud` | Official Ubuntu image project |
| `acceleratorType` | `nvidia-tesla-a100` | GPU type (replace with RTX A6000 if available) |
| `acceleratorCount` | `1` | Number of GPUs |
| `tags` | `http-server,https-server` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic |
| `metadata` | `startup-script` | Optional custom startup script |

---

### Bottom Line

- **Use `gcloud compute instances create`** for quick, interactive creation.  
- **Use the REST API** if you need programmatic control or integration into other systems.  
- **Replace the GPU type** with the exact one you want once it becomes available on Google Cloud.  

Happy computing!
